purpose: Trace the reported low current-image valid fraction in Park City review windows W005 and W023.
method: Read only the existing Park City four-band NAIP raster from the preserved original checkout. Recreated each 213x213 pixel, 0.6 m window using the paired-imagery screen center and raster transform; used boundless reads with the same rasterio read_masks behavior as the screen. No original checkout files were modified.

source.rasterio_warning: NodataShadowWarning: the dataset nodata attribute shadows the alpha band; masks are determined by nodata.

finding: Both windows have the same column position and are partly east of the raster's x maximum. The screen's 23.0047% mask-valid fraction is explained by 49/213 columns inside the dataset footprint, not by internal invalid pixels in these windows. The in-footprint pixels are valid and nonzero. This resolves the two window-specific coverage questions.
remaining_limits: This does not resolve nodata/alpha semantics for other parts of the mosaic or prove how every training tensor and label weight treats out-of-footprint pixels.
Do not infer that any affected trail pixels should be excluded from evaluation until source footprint, raster mask, tensor, and label-mask overlap are compared.
